newsitem.title: USA: Ultramar sees $25 mln savings in '97.
newsitem.headline: Ultramar sees $25 mln savings in '97.

text.p: Ultramar Diamond Shamrock Corp Friday said it sees at least $25 million in 1997 savings and in excess of $75 million in savings in 1998 as a result of the merger of Ultramar Corp and Diamond Shamrock Inc in 1996.
It said the firm has already exceeded projected savings in such areas as insurance and interest expense reductions.
The company also said it expects to increase sales of both wholesale and retail petroleum products in the Southwest.

"In our key Arizona markets, Ultramar Diamond Shamrock has a unique strategic advantage in being able to supply high-quality petroleum products from either its California or Texas refineries," said Ultramar Diamond Shamrock chairman and chief executive Roger Hemminghaus.
On Thursday, the company reported a 1996 fourth quarter loss of $118.9 million or $1.61 per share against a net loss for the year ended December 31, 1996 of $35.9 million or $0.54 per share.

Hemminghaus commented, "Results were negatively impacted by industry-wide weak refining margins. Retail marketing margins in the Southwest were particularly poor during the fourth quarter due to intense competitive pricing."
